literal: Through the generations they did not abandon their craft; therefore in early Wei the calligraphy of the Cui and Lu clans was prized.
idiomatic: Their craft never lapsed—so in early Wei the Cui and Lu scripts were prized.

literal: Hong himself, unless it was an imperial document for the court or letters and proclamations for the four directions, at first did not lightly touch brush—thus the world has no surviving writings of his.
idiomatic: Unless it was court edict or dispatch to the realm, Hong would not lightly take brush—so no writings of his survive.

literal: He was especially skilled in cursive and clerical script, a model for the age; running and draft were supremely fine and subtle, yet no traces remain.
idiomatic: He excelled in cursive and clerical script, the age's model; running and draft were exquisite—yet no traces remain.

literal: At first, because of the chaos of Fu Jian's house, Hong wished to flee south to the Yangtze but was seized by Zhang Yuan; his original plan was not fulfilled.
idiomatic: When Fu Jian's house fell into chaos Hong meant to flee south but Zhang Yuan seized him. The plan failed.

literal: He therefore composed a poem to mourn himself, but it did not circulate in the age—likely from fear of guilt.
idiomatic: He wrote a poem to mourn himself, but it did not circulate—likely from fear of punishment.

literal: When Hao was executed, Central Secretariat Gentleman Gao Yun received an edict to collect Hao's household books and first saw this poem; Yun knew its meaning.
idiomatic: At Hao's death Gao Yun was ordered to collect Hao's books and first saw this poem. Yun understood it.

literal: Yun's grandson Chuo copied it into Yun's collected works.
idiomatic: Yun's grandson Chuo copied it into Yun's collected works.

literal: At the start, Hong's father Qian had written for his elder brother Hun and others a eulogy in his own hand on herbal medicine; in Yan chang's early years Compiling Assistant Wang Zunyue bought books in the market and happened to obtain it.
idiomatic: At first Hong's father Qian had written in his own hand for his brother Hun a eulogy on herbal medicine. In early Yan chang Wang Zunyue bought books in the market and found it.

literal: Nearly two hundred years had passed; he treasured the calligraphic trace and hid it in secret.
idiomatic: Nearly two hundred years had passed. He treasured the trace and kept it hidden.

literal: In Wuding, Zunyue's son Songnian was about to give it to Cui Jishu, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; many copied it by rubbing.
idiomatic: In Wuding Zunyue's son Songnian meant to give it to Cui Jishu of the Yellow Gate. Many made rubbings.

literal: Left Household Grandee Yao Yuanbiao was famed in the age for skill in calligraphy; seeing Qian's writing, he thought it surpassed Hao's.
idiomatic: Yao Yuanbiao, famed for calligraphy, saw Qian's hand and thought it surpassed Hao's.

literal: Hong's younger brother Hui, styled Xuanyou, had literary talent in youth and was famed together with Bohai's Gao Yan.
idiomatic: Hong's brother Hui, styled Xuanyou, had literary talent in youth and was famed with Bohai's Gao Yan.

literal: He held the post of Director of the Secretariat and was granted the title Marquis of Beiqiu.
idiomatic: He was Director of the Secretariat and Marquis of Beiqiu.

literal: Prince of Le'an Fan garrisoned Chang'an and chose men of old virtue to accompany Fan; Hui was made Vice General of Pacifying the West and acting Tutor to the Prince of Le'an, advanced to Duke of Jinan.
idiomatic: Prince of Le'an Fan held Chang'an and chose elders to accompany him. Hui was made Vice General of Pacifying the West and acting tutor to the prince, advanced to Duke of Jinan.

literal: In government Hui kept to the great pattern and did not attend to small matters.
idiomatic: In office Hui kept the great pattern and left small matters alone.

literal: By nature he loved human relations.
idiomatic: He loved human worth by nature.

literal: Receiving guests, he might speak of his whole life or discuss the Way and righteousness, instructing the young—without ceasing all day.
idiomatic: He received guests—talking of his life, of the Way, teaching the young—all day without stop.

literal: Because of illness he was summoned back to the capital and died; posthumous name Duke Yuan. Men of his kind all sighed.
idiomatic: Ill, he was recalled to the capital and died. Posthumous name Duke Yuan. Scholars mourned.

literal: At the start, Qinghe's Cui Kuan traced his ancestry to Tong, who followed Jin's Prince of Nanyang Bao in fleeing to Longyou and then served Western Liang and the Juqu house.
idiomatic: Qinghe's Cui Kuan traced to Tong, who followed Prince of Nanyang Bao south to Longyou and served Western Liang and the Juqu.

literal: Tong begot Pou, styled Bozong, who was often stirred with longing for the eastern lands.
idiomatic: Tong begot Pou, styled Bozong, often stirred with longing for the east.

literal: He often sighed: "Wind and rain dark, the cock crows unceasing—that is what I hope for!"
idiomatic: He often sighed: "Wind and rain, yet the cock crows—that is what I hope for!"

literal: " When Taiwu toured the west, Pou mustered men of shared purpose and sent his son Kuan to offer allegiance.
idiomatic: " When Taiwu toured west, Pou rallied like-minded men and sent his son Kuan to submit.

literal: Taiwu was pleased and appointed Kuan Magistrate of Qiyang, granting the title Baron of Yanshui.
idiomatic: Taiwu was pleased. Kuan was made Magistrate of Qiyang and Baron of Yanshui.

literal: He sent an envoy to go west with Kuan and comfort those newly attached.
idiomatic: An envoy went west with Kuan to comfort the newly attached.

literal: Pou was summoned to the capital but died before arriving.
idiomatic: Pou was summoned to the capital but died on the way.

literal: Wencheng, because Pou's loyalty was clear in the former court, posthumously made him Inspector of Liangzhou and Duke of Wuling, posthumous name Yuan.
idiomatic: Wencheng, for Pou's loyalty in the former reign, posthumously made him Inspector of Liangzhou and Duke of Wuling, posthumous name Yuan.

literal: Kuan, styled Jingren, returned to the capital, was enfeoffed Viscount of Anguo, and held the post of Governor of Hongnong.
idiomatic: Kuan, styled Jingren, returned, was made Viscount of Anguo, and Governor of Hongnong.

literal: At first, when Kuan offered allegiance he met Hao; Hao matched him in age and received him with deep courtesy.
idiomatic: When Kuan first submitted he met Hao. Hao matched him in age and received him warmly.

literal: When Hao was executed, as a distant clan who had come from afar, he alone was not implicated.
idiomatic: At Hao's death, a distant clan come from afar, he alone escaped punishment.

literal: He then made his home in Wucheng, dwelling on the old site of Sikong Lin, with one son continuing Hao's line.
idiomatic: He settled in Wucheng on Sikong Lin's old ground, with one son to continue Hao's line.

literal: With Hao's brother Lan's wife of the Feng clan he tended each other like kin.
idiomatic: He and Hao's brother Lan's wife Feng tended each other like kin.

literal: Later Kuan inherited the title Duke of Wuling and was garrison commander of Shancheng.
idiomatic: Later Kuan inherited Duke of Wuling and was garrison commander of Shancheng.

literal: The Three Gorges country was rugged; men often robbed and raided.
idiomatic: The Three Gorges were rugged. Men often robbed.

literal: Kuan by nature was witty and humorous; he drew in powerful local men and old bandit chiefs and joined with them.
idiomatic: Kuan was witty. He drew in local powers and bandit chiefs and befriended them.

literal: He poured out his breast in reception, not rejecting the smallest detail; none failed to be moved by his spirit.
idiomatic: He received them with open heart, not refusing the smallest courtesy. All were moved by his spirit.

literal: At the time officials had no salary but took their support from others; Kuan was skilled at soothing and gathering them, inviting gifts and presents—he received much, yet those who gave bore no resentment.
idiomatic: Officials had no salary then and lived on others' gifts. Kuan soothed and gathered them, accepting much—yet givers bore no grudge.

literal: Hengnong moreover produced lacquer, wax, bamboo, and timber in abundance; the road connected southward and trade came and went—his household was rich while the common people were content.
idiomatic: Hengnong was rich in lacquer, wax, bamboo, and timber. Trade ran south. His house was rich and the people content.

literal: Among the garrisons he was called able in government.
idiomatic: Among garrisons he was called able in government.

literal: When he left his post, men pursued him with longing; more than three hundred went to court with memorials.
idiomatic: When he left, men followed with longing. More than three hundred memorialized at court.

literal: At death he left instructions for a plain burial, enshrouded in timely dress.
idiomatic: He ordered a plain burial in timely dress.

literal: His eldest son Chang, styled Gongshi, inherited the title, reduced by precedent to marquis, and was Chancellor of Pingyuan.
idiomatic: Eldest son Chang, styled Gongshi, inherited—reduced by rule to marquis—and was Chancellor of Pingyuan.

literal: Chang's nature was narrow and hasty; he and the inspector Yang Chun repeatedly memorialized against each other, and Chang was dismissed from office.
idiomatic: Chang was narrow and hasty. He and Inspector Yang Chun denounced each other in memorials. Chang was dismissed.

literal: In Xuanwu's early reign he was Governor of Julu.
idiomatic: In early Xuanwu he was Governor of Julu.

literal: At Fei's rebellion, Chang was hidden by Huangmu Army Commander Han Wenshu.
idiomatic: At Fei's rebellion Chang was hidden by Han Wenshu, commander of the Huangmu Army.

literal: His household was entirely registered and confiscated; only Chang's wife Li, as niece of a princess, with her own servants, fields, and houses—more than two hundred mouths—was spared.
idiomatic: His household was confiscated. Only his wife Li, a princess's niece, with her servants, fields, and houses—more than two hundred souls—was spared.

literal: In Zhengguang, when the general amnesty lifted bonds, Chang recovered his commandery marquisate and died as Governor of Zhao commandery.
idiomatic: In Zhengguang, when bonds were lifted, Chang recovered his marquisate and died as Governor of Zhao commandery.

literal: Chang's younger brother Zhong, styled Gonglu, was a Court Gentleman.
idiomatic: Brother Zhong, styled Gonglu, was Court Gentleman.

literal: At Fei's rebellion, because he had been adopted out he was pardoned.
idiomatic: At Fei's rebellion, adopted out, he was pardoned.

literal: He held the posts of Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, Grandee of the Golden Purple and Bright Light, and Rectifier of Ji.
idiomatic: He was Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, Grandee of Golden Purple and Bright Light, and Rectifier of Ji.

literal: After Chang died, Zhong coveted his wealth and falsely claimed Chang's sons Ji and three others were not legitimate heirs; lawsuits dragged on for years, and gentlemen despised him.
idiomatic: After Chang died Zhong coveted his wealth and claimed Chang's sons Ji and two others were not true heirs. Lawsuits ran for years. Gentlemen despised him.

literal: Erzhu Shilong as Minister of the Masters of Writing memorialized to strip him of office, never to be ranked again.
idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong as Minister of the Masters of Writing stripped him of office for life.

literal: Fei loved learning and had literary talent; he was Recorder of Prince of Jingzhao Yu and rebelled with Yu and was executed.
idiomatic: Fei loved learning and had literary talent. He was recorder to Prince of Jingzhao Yu, rebelled with Yu, and was executed.

literal: In Hong's same commandery, Dong Mi.
idiomatic: In Hong's commandery lived Dong Mi.

literal: Mi's father Jing, with Cui Kangshi of the same commandery and Huo Yuan of Guangyang, were all famed as great scholars, their names spreading over Liaohai.
idiomatic: Mi's father Jing, with Cui Kangshi and Guangyang's Huo Yuan, were great scholars famed across Liaohai.

literal: Mi loved learning and inherited his father's craft.
idiomatic: Mi loved learning and inherited his father's craft.

literal: When Zhongshan was pacified he entered court, was appointed Gentleman of the Ceremonial Office, and composed the rites for court audience, feasts, suburban altars, and the altars of soil and grain.
idiomatic: When Zhongshan fell he entered court as Gentleman of the Ceremonial Office and wrote rites for audience, feast, suburban sacrifice, and altars of soil and grain.

literal: Zhang Gun, styled Honglong, was a man of Jieyang, Shanggu.
idiomatic: Zhang Gun, styled Honglong, was from Jieyang in Shanggu.

literal: His grandfather Yi and father Zhuo both held the post of governor.
idiomatic: Grandfather Yi and father Zhuo were both governors.

literal: Gun was sincere and solid, loved learning, and had literary talent.
idiomatic: Gun was sincere, loved learning, and had literary talent.

literal: When Daowu was Prince of Dai, Gun was chosen as Left Chief Clerk.
idiomatic: When Daowu was Prince of Dai, Gun was chosen Left Chief Clerk.

literal: He followed in pursuit of the Rouran for five or six hundred li.
idiomatic: He followed pursuit of the Rouran five or six hundred li.

literal: The various tribal chiefs, taking advantage of Yan's report that grain was exhausted, said it was not fitting to go deep.
idiomatic: Tribal chiefs, hearing Yan say grain was gone, said they should not go deep.

literal: The emperor asked Gun: "If we kill the spare horses, is there food for three days?"
idiomatic: The emperor asked Gun: "Slaughter the spare horses—food for three days?"

literal: " All said it was enough.
idiomatic: " All said yes.

literal: The emperor therefore doubled the march and caught up at south of Bed Mountain on the broad red desert, inflicting a great defeat.
idiomatic: He doubled the march and caught them south of Bed Mountain on the broad red desert and broke them utterly.

literal: Afterward the emperor asked Gun: "You outsiders—did you know my earlier meaning about three days' grain?"
idiomatic: Afterward he asked Gun: "You outsiders—did you grasp my three-days' grain?"

literal: The Rouran run for days; their livestock lose drink and must halt at water.
idiomatic: The Rouran run for days. Their herds lose drink and must halt at water.

literal: Calculating their route, three days is enough to reach them.
idiomatic: Count their route—three days is enough.

literal: Light cavalry arriving suddenly takes them unawares; they are sure to scatter in alarm—that is how the momentum runs."
idiomatic: Light horse arrives unawares—they scatter. That is the momentum."

literal: " The tribal chiefs heard it and all said: "Sacred stratagem—beyond what we could reach."
idiomatic: " The chiefs said: "Sacred stratagem—beyond us."

literal: " Gun often participated in great deliberations and would tell others: "Our lord's heaven-born talent is outstanding; he is sure to embrace the six directions.
idiomatic: " Gun often joined great counsel and told others: "Our lord's talent is heaven-born. He will embrace the six directions.

literal: One who meets the season of wind and cloud yet does not build leaping achievement is no true hero."
idiomatic: Meet wind and cloud and build no soaring merit—that is no hero."

literal: He therefore pledged his name and gave his utmost loyalty.
idiomatic: He pledged his name and served with utmost loyalty.

literal: At the time Liu Xian's territory was broad and his troops strong, spanning the northern borderlands; it happened that his brothers were estranged and mutually suspicious.
idiomatic: Liu Xian held broad land and strong troops across the north. His brothers quarreled and suspected each other.

literal: Gun said to Daowu: "Xian's will is great and his intent high; now, while their inner rift is open, we ought to strike swiftly."
idiomatic: Gun told Daowu: "Xian's will is great. Strike now while they split within."

literal: The emperor followed him and broke and drove off Xian.
idiomatic: The emperor listened and broke Xian and drove him off.

literal: He also followed in defeating He Na.
idiomatic: He also followed in defeating He Na.

literal: Daowu ascended Wuju Mountain for a feast; his attendants asked to pile stones into a peak to record merit, and he ordered Gun to compose the text.
idiomatic: Daowu feasted on Wuju Mountain. Attendants asked to pile stones as a peak to record merit. Gun was ordered to write the text.

literal: When Murong Bao came to raid, Gun said to Daowu: "Bao rides on the merit of Huatai and, because of his victory at Changzi, exhausts wealth and strength—it is hard to contend with him in the spear. We ought to show a weak army to swell his heart."
idiomatic: When Murong Bao raided, Gun said: "Bao rides Huatai's merit and Changzi's victory. He has spent wealth and strength—hard to meet in the spear. Show a weak army and swell his heart."

literal: The emperor followed him and indeed broke Bao at Canhe.
idiomatic: The emperor listened and broke Bao at Canhe.

literal: He was transferred to Gentlemen Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: He was made Gentlemen Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

literal: On Daowu's southern campaign he halted at Zhongshan; Gun sent Bao a letter explaining success and failure.
idiomatic: On Daowu's southern campaign he halted at Zhongshan. Gun sent Bao a letter on success and failure.

literal: Bao saw the letter and was greatly afraid; he then fled to Helong.
idiomatic: Bao read it and was greatly afraid. He fled to Helong.

literal: After Zhongshan was taken, he was admitted to the Eight Discussions, appointed Inspector of Youzhou, enfeoffed Marquis of Linwei, and the common people were settled under him.
idiomatic: After Zhongshan fell he entered the Eight Discussions, was Inspector of Youzhou and Marquis of Linwei. The people were settled.

literal: In Tianxing's early years he was recalled to the capital.
idiomatic: In early Tianxing he was recalled to the capital.

literal: Later, because he and Cui Cheng answered Jin general Xi Hui's letter off the mark, he was demoted to Chief Clerk of the Minister of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Later he and Cui Cheng answered Jin general Xi Hui's letter badly and he was demoted to chief clerk of the Minister of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Gun met the realm at the founding of enterprise; at first he was trusted for talent and stratagem, serving with an open heart without regard for suspicion.
idiomatic: Gun met the realm at its founding and was first trusted for talent, serving openly without fear of suspicion.

literal: Daowu once asked Gun about men of the southern provinces; Gun and Lu Pu were from the same commandery and he repeatedly praised and recommended Pu.
idiomatic: Daowu once asked Gun about southern men. Gun and Lu Pu were townsmen. He praised Pu again and again.

literal: He had also never known Cui Cheng but heard his reputation and praised him.
idiomatic: He had never met Cui Cheng but heard his fame and praised him.

literal: When Zhongshan was pacified, Lu Pu gathered a faction to rebel and Cui Cheng's answering letter was not compliant—both contrary to what he had said—and therefore he resented them.
idiomatic: When Zhongshan fell Lu Pu rebelled and Cui Cheng's reply was not compliant—both against his word—and he resented them.

literal: Gun passed seventy; he closed his gates and kept quiet, holding the classics in hand, collating and correcting errors.
idiomatic: Past seventy Gun closed his gates, held the classics, and collated errors.

literal: He loved worthy men and skillfully guided without weariness; gentlemen for this held him high.
idiomatic: He loved worthy men and taught without weariness. Gentlemen honored him.

literal: In the second year of Yongxing he died.
idiomatic: In Yongxing year two he died.

literal: Later Taiwu's empress posthumously recorded old merit and sent the Grand Herald to his tomb with patent, posthumously making him Grand Preceptor, posthumous name Duke Wenkang.
idiomatic: Later Taiwu's empress recorded old merit and sent the Grand Herald to his tomb with patent, posthumously Grand Preceptor, posthumous name Duke Wenkang.

literal: His son Du in youth had learning and esteem, inherited the title Marquis of Linwei, and died as Grand Provisioner of the Central Capital.
idiomatic: Son Du in youth had learning, inherited Marquis of Linwei, and died as Grand Provisioner of the Central Capital.

literal: Du's son Baize at eleven suffered his mother's mourning and was known for filial piety.
idiomatic: Du's son Baize at eleven mourned his mother and was known for filial piety.

literal: Grown, he was broadly learned.
idiomatic: Grown, he was broadly learned.

literal: In Wencheng's early reign he was appointed Attendant of the Palace Bureau and greatly favored.
idiomatic: In early Wencheng he was Attendant of the Palace Bureau and greatly favored.

literal: Baize's original name was Zhongkui; Xianwen granted the name Baize and took his daughter as consort.
idiomatic: Baize's original name was Zhongkui. Xianwen granted the name Baize and took his daughter as consort.

literal: He went out as Inspector of Yongzhou.
idiomatic: He went out as Inspector of Yongzhou.
